Path: changing a running app without code — an accessible name reaches the DOM | 缺项 (`ariaAttrs` writes `aria-arialabel`) | P2

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:studio` · `pm:queue`. Direction: map the spec's `AriaProps` keys through the shared aria reader

Triage: lands in `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx` (the file-local `ariaAttrs`, spread at six call sites by `element:text` / `button` / `image` / `number`) ⇒ `domain:ui`.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T06:53Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why p2.** A declared accessible-name channel is silently dropped. An author who sets `aria.ariaLabel` gets `aria-arialabel`, which no assistive technology reads, and no error. That is declared ≠ enforced (ADR-0049) on four core elements, for plain strings too. It is runs-but-wrong.

**Direction.**
- Replace the file-local prefixing with the shared aria reader the other renderers use (`resolveAriaProps`, named in PR objectui#10855). It maps `ariaLabel` → `aria-label`, `ariaDescribedBy` → `aria-describedby` and `role` → `role`, and resolves an `I18nLabel` against the UI language. ⛔ No second mapping table in `elements.tsx`.
- The `[object Object]` half for a per-locale map is objectui#10993's census row. It is fixed by the same reader, so note it there when this lands.
- **Pins:** a plain string and a locale map on one element render `aria-label`, with a lit control on a renderer that already applies the name.

- `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx`: the file-local `ariaAttrs` prefixing is replaced by the shared aria reader the other renderers use (`resolveAriaProps`, named in PR objectui#10855). It maps `ariaLabel` → `aria-label`, `ariaDescribedBy` → `aria-describedby` and `role` → `role`, and resolves an `I18nLabel` against the UI language. This covers all six `ariaAttrs(` call sites (`element:text`, `button`, `image`, `number`).
- Pins: a plain string and a locale map on one element render `aria-label`, with a lit control on a renderer that already uses the shared reader.
- A changeset.

⛔ No second mapping table in `elements.tsx`, and no change to the spec's `AriaProps` or to any schema.
Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (TIER_DEFAULT, objectstack `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:12692` at `81137630`)
Clause-②: no
Why no: a renderer now honours a key its published schema already declares and accepts (ADR-0049 declared ⇒ enforced); no accept set, type or documented contract moves.

Dispatch note: under the maintainer's 「当前没有fable，你可以派 opus 卡」 (this seat's chat, 2026-09-29T01:00Z), this card needs no review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat verifies the changeset prose itself at the ACCEPT.

## Released to triage: the graded route does not hold, measured · `domain:ui` seat #1 · 2026-09-29T07:26Z

`session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` (`os-steve`). The dev stopped under the claim's "Stop on breach" and wrote no code. Its report is `os-dev-report` on this card (status `needs_decision`). The branch `claude/issue-11051-element-aria-reader` was pushed empty as the claim marker.

Release: `session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk` · cause: triage's Direction (`5885230119`) names a reader that cannot carry these elements' aria, and every working route breaks either that Direction's ⛔ or the claim's surface · destination: `pm:queue` with `pm:retriage`. The claim `5885494383` is spent. The route is an API choice, and it is not this seat's to make.

**The defect is confirmed.** It was measured through the real `SchemaRenderer`, under en and zh, at objectui `37a19d4e0`:
- `properties.aria.ariaLabel: 'Plain name'` on `element:text`, `button`, `image` and `number` renders `aria-arialabel="Plain name"` and no `aria-label`.
- A locale map renders `aria-arialabel="[object Object]"`.
- `ariaDescribedBy` renders `aria-ariadescribedby`.

**Why `resolveAriaProps` cannot be the route.** Each point was measured:
1. It is module-private in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`. `SchemaRenderer` calls it once per node and injects the result as React props, which the `element:*` renderers never read.
2. It reads the FLAT `BaseSchema` keys (`ariaLabel`, `ariaDescribedBy`, `role`). The installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 declares a NESTED `aria` (`AriaPropsSchema`) on these four elements' props.
3. It resolves with `resolveKeyedI18nLabel`, the keyed vocabulary, which returns `undefined` for an inline locale map. Measured: a flat locale map on a lit-control `container` renders no `aria-label` in en or zh. So this route would turn `[object Object]` into no name at all, and the Direction's own locale-map pin would fail. The repo splits the two vocabularies on purpose (objectui#4580 Q2-B; the `BaseSchema.ariaLabel` and `PageSchema.aria` docblocks).

Two readers already map the spec's nested `AriaProps` and resolve a locale map against the UI language. ListView does it inline in `plugin-list`, and `useRecordAriaProps` does it in `plugin-detail`'s `recordComponentAria.ts`; both use the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` with `useDisplayLocale()`. Neither can be imported from `@object-ui/components`, which sits below both plugins.

**Routes the dev measured.** Its recommendation is A2 with Q2-a.
- **A.** Lift one nested-bag reader into `@object-ui/react` and export it beside `resolveAriaProps`, which stays the flat keyed reader. `elements.tsx` calls it at its five call sites and holds no table.
  - This adds a **new public export**, which the seat reads as `Clause-②: yes`: it widens a published surface. It would then need a review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
  - A1 also migrates ListView and `useRecordAriaProps` in the same PR. A2 files those as follow-ups.
  - Q2 is the name and shape: a pure `resolveInlineAriaProps(aria, locale)`, or a hook.
- **B.** Map the three keys locally in `elements.tsx`, with the same convention. It is the smallest change, but it is the third copy of the convention and reverses the Direction's ⛔ "No second mapping table in `elements.tsx`".
- **C.** Widen `SchemaRenderer`'s `resolveAriaProps` to read the nested bag. It has the largest blast radius: it changes the props injected into every aria-bearing node, and mixes the two vocabularies objectui#4580 split.

**What the seat needs:** a ruling on the route (A, B or C), and for A the export's name and shape.

**Facts that hold under any route:**
- `role` is a spec key and stays.
- The old helper's pass-through of raw `aria-*` keys, and its accidental `aria: { label }` → `aria-label`, have no producer; `git grep` finds none in objectui or objectstack. The spec refuses both shapes (`unrecognized_keys`).

**A related finding for the same decision, measured once:** `{ type: 'page', aria: { ariaLabel: 'Page name' } }` renders no `aria-label` anywhere. `PageSchema.aria` is declared ("Aligned with `@objectstack/spec` `AriaPropsSchema`") and read by nothing. A shared nested reader (route A) would serve the page root too.

Correction to the card: `elements.tsx` has five `ariaAttrs(` call sites plus the definition, not six call sites.
